conditions: DC and timing limits for Standard-mode (Sm, 100 kbit/s), Fast-mode (Fm, 400 kbit/s) and Fast-mode Plus (Fm+, 1 Mbit/s) I2C-bus devices at VDD = 2 V to 5.5 V unless a fact says otherwise; VIL/VIH levels are referenced to VDD (VIL max = 0.3 VDD, VIH min = 0.7 VDD). Rise/fall times are measured between 30 % and 70 % of VDD (Figure 38). These facts do NOT cover Hs-mode (Table 12), UFm, or SMBus limits.

rise_time_max_s.applies_to: I2C-bus SDA and SCL lines, Fast-mode (400 kbit/s)
rise_time_max_s.condition: maximum rise time tr from 0.3 VDD to 0.7 VDD, Cb <= 400 pF, measured 30 %/70 % (Table 11); Standard-mode max is 1000 ns and Fast-mode Plus max is 120 ns - the per-mode keys below are normative, this key is the Fast-mode value
rise_time_max_s.source: UM10204, Table 11 (printed p. 43) and Figure 38 (printed p. 45)

rise_time_max_s_standard.condition: maximum rise time, Cb <= 400 pF, no minimum rise time stated

rise_time_min_s_fast.condition: minimum rise time 20 ns (Fast-mode only); Standard-mode and Fm+ state no minimum rise time

fall_time_max_s_standard.condition: maximum fall time tf of the bus lines, Cb <= 400 pF; the output-stage fall time tof is separately limited to 250 ns

fall_time_max_s_fast.condition: maximum fall time of the bus lines, Cb <= 400 pF; minimum fall time is 20 x (VDD / 5.5 V) ns

fall_time_max_s_fast_plus.condition: maximum fall time of the bus lines, Cb <= 550 pF; minimum fall time is 20 x (VDD / 5.5 V) ns (backwards compatibility with Fast-mode)

fall_time_min_formula.value: 20 x (VDD / 5.5 V) ns for Fast-mode and Fast-mode Plus (no minimum for Standard-mode)
fall_time_min_formula.applies_to: I2C-bus SDA/SCL, Fast-mode and Fast-mode Plus
fall_time_min_formula.condition: minimum fall time, measured 70 %/30 % of VDD; the formula scales with the actual VDD

bus_cap_max_f.applies_to: each I2C-bus line, Standard-mode and Fast-mode
bus_cap_max_f.condition: maximum capacitive load for each bus line Cb = 400 pF in Standard-mode and Fast-mode; Fast-mode Plus allows 550 pF - the per-mode keys below are normative, this key is the Sm/Fm value

bus_cap_max_f_standard.condition: maximum capacitive load for each bus line, 400 pF

bus_cap_max_f_fast.condition: maximum capacitive load for each bus line, 400 pF

bus_cap_max_f_fast_plus.condition: maximum capacitive load for each bus line, 550 pF

vol_max_v.applies_to: I2C-bus SDA/SCL output stage (open-drain or open-collector), Standard/Fast/Fast-mode Plus
vol_max_v.condition: maximum LOW-level output voltage VOL1 at IOL = 3 mA sink current, VDD > 2 V

vol_max_v_at_6ma_fast.condition: maximum LOW-level output voltage 0.6 V at IOL = 6 mA, the current required to drive the full 400 pF bus load at 400 kHz (Table 10 note 4)
vol_max_v_at_6ma_fast.source: UM10204, Table 10 IOL (printed p. 43) and note 4 (printed pp. 43-44)

vol2_max_vdd_ratio.applies_to: I2C-bus output stage, Fast-mode and Fast-mode Plus with VDD <= 2 V
vol2_max_vdd_ratio.condition: maximum LOW-level output voltage VOL2 = 0.2 x VDD at IOL = 2 mA sink current (VDD <= 2 V)

iol_min_a.applies_to: I2C-bus output stage, Standard-mode and Fast-mode
iol_min_a.condition: minimum LOW-level output sink current at VOL = 0.4 V (VDD > 2 V); Fast-mode additionally needs 6 mA at VOL = 0.6 V for full 400 pF bus load

iol_min_a_fast_full_load.condition: minimum sink current at VOL = 0.6 V required to drive full bus load (400 pF) at 400 kHz
iol_min_a_fast_full_load.source: UM10204, Table 10 IOL and note 4 (printed pp. 43-44)

iol_min_a_fast_plus.condition: minimum LOW-level output sink current at VOL = 0.4 V; Fm+ devices drive 20 mA

vil_max_vdd_ratio.condition: maximum LOW-level input voltage VIL = 0.3 x VDD (absolute minimum -0.5 V); legacy Standard-mode devices with fixed 1.5 V/3.0 V levels are excluded by note 1

vih_min_vdd_ratio.condition: minimum HIGH-level input voltage VIH = 0.7 x VDD

vhys_min_vdd_ratio.applies_to: I2C-bus SDA/SCL inputs, Fast-mode and Fast-mode Plus
vhys_min_vdd_ratio.condition: minimum hysteresis of the Schmitt-trigger inputs 0.05 x VDD; Standard-mode states no hysteresis value

noise_margin_low_min_vdd_ratio.applies_to: I2C-bus, each connected device, Standard/Fast/Fast-mode Plus
noise_margin_low_min_vdd_ratio.condition: minimum LOW-level noise margin VnL = 0.1 x VDD (including hysteresis)

noise_margin_high_min_vdd_ratio.applies_to: I2C-bus, each connected device, Standard/Fast/Fast-mode Plus
noise_margin_high_min_vdd_ratio.condition: minimum HIGH-level noise margin VnH = 0.2 x VDD (including hysteresis)

f_scl_max_hz_standard.condition: maximum SCL clock frequency 100 kbit/s; minimum 0 Hz but the specification notes 10 kHz minimum to prevent bus lock-up

spike_suppression_max_s.applies_to: I2C-bus SDA/SCL inputs, Fast-mode and Fast-mode Plus
spike_suppression_max_s.condition: maximum pulse width of spikes suppressed by the input filter, 50 ns (spikes shorter than this are filtered); Standard-mode states no input-filter value

pin_cap_max_f.applies_to: I2C-bus SDA/SCL I/O pin, Standard/Fast/Fast-mode Plus
pin_cap_max_f.condition: maximum capacitance for each I/O pin Ci = 10 pF (special-purpose devices such as switches may exceed this)

bus_free_time_min_s_standard.condition: minimum bus free time tBUF between STOP and START; Fast-mode 1.3 us, Fast-mode Plus 0.5 us

rp_max_formula.value: Rp(max) = tr / (0.8473 x Cb) for every mode, where tr is the mode's maximum rise time from Table 11 and Cb is the estimated total bus capacitance (0.8473 = t2 - t1 for the 0.3 VDD to 0.7 VDD transition of an RC charge)
rp_max_formula.applies_to: I2C-bus pull-up resistor sizing, Standard/Fast/Fast-mode Plus
rp_max_formula.condition: first-order RC charge from 0.3 VDD to 0.7 VDD; Section 7.1 equation 1; a real bus with series resistors or non-ideal edges needs a guard band

rp_min_formula.value: Rp(min) = (VDD - VOL(max)) / IOL where IOL is 3 mA for Standard/Fast-mode and 20 mA for Fast-mode Plus (VOL(max) = 0.4 V)
rp_min_formula.applies_to: I2C-bus pull-up resistor sizing, Standard/Fast/Fast-mode Plus
rp_min_formula.condition: Section 7.1 equation 2; the resistor must not be so small that a device cannot pull the line below VOL(max)

rp_min_example_ohm.condition: datasheet worked example: VDD = 5 V +/-10 % (worst case 5.5 V), VOL(max) = 0.4 V at 3 mA => Rp(min) = (5.5 - 0.4) / 0.003 = 1.7 kohm

unknown_facts: No bus-timing numbers apply to Hs-mode (Table 12) or UltraFast-mode; a design that needs those modes must use Table 12 / the UFm section, not this file.

The specification gives no numeric maximum for total bus capacitance above which communication is impossible at a given frequency; 400 pF / 550 pF are the specified Cb limits, and Section 7.2 only describes techniques (lower fSCL, stronger drivers, buffers) for exceeding them.
No single 'guaranteed bus frequency' can be derived from these limits alone: fSCL also depends on tLOW/tHIGH of the slowest connected device, which are per-part datasheet values.
The capacitance limit for special-purpose devices (multiplexers/switches) may exceed the 10 pF pin value and is not covered here.
No pull-up resistor tolerance/ESR (self-heating) treatment is given in UM10204; the resistor tolerance and temperature coefficient must come from the resistor datasheet.
notes: Verified against UM10204 Rev. 7.0 (1 October 2021) served at the URL above on 2026-10-27. Revision 7.0 is the current release listed in the document revision history; it renamed master/slave to controller/target and updated Table 5, but the Table 10/Table 11 limits used here are unchanged in substance from Rev. 6. Table 10 is the I/O-stage table (VIL/VIH, VOL1/VOL2, IOL, tof, tSP, Ci) and Table 11 is the bus-line table (fSCL, tr, tf, Cb, timing, noise margins), both on printed pp. 43-44. This file deliberately carries per-mode keys so the open-drain pull-up module can use the coefficient of the actual interface (Standard 1000 ns, Fast 300 ns, Fm+ 120 ns) instead of one universal factor; the un-suffixed rise_time_max_s / bus_cap_max_f / vol_max_v keys are convenience aliases whose conditions state which mode they describe.
